sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvanirghoṣo mahān āsīd viśāṃ pate stanatāṃ kūjatāṃ caiva manuṣyagajavājinām
english: Then a great din of the Gāṇḍīva arose, O lord of peoples, mingled with the bellowing and the moaning of men and elephants and horses.

sanskrit: kuñjarāś ca hatā rājan prādravaṃs te samantataḥ aśvāś ca paryadhāvanta hatārohā diśo daśa
english: The elephants, stricken, O king, fled away on every side, and the horses, their riders slain, ran scattering in all ten directions.

sanskrit: rathā hīnā mahārāja rathibhir vājibhis tathā gandharvanagarākārā dṛśyante sma sahasraśaḥ
english: Chariots bereft of their warriors and their steeds, O great king, were seen by the thousands, looking like the phantom cities of the gandharvas.

sanskrit: aśvārohā mahārāja dhāvamānās tatas tataḥ tatra tatraiva dṛśyante patitāḥ pārthasāyakaiḥ
english: The horsemen, O great king, fleeing this way and that, were seen falling here and there, struck down by Pārtha's arrows.

sanskrit: tasmin kṣaṇe pāṇḍavasya bāhvor balam adṛśyata yat sādino vāraṇāṃś ca rathāṃś caiko 'jayad yudhi
english: In that moment the strength of the Pāṇḍava's arms was made manifest, for alone in battle he conquered cavalry and elephants and chariots.

sanskrit: tatas tryaṅgeṇa mahatā balena bharatarṣabha dṛṣṭvā parivṛtaṃ rājan bhīmasenaḥ kirīṭinam
english: Then, O bull of the Bharatas, seeing the Diademed One surrounded by a great threefold host, O king, Bhīmasena—

sanskrit: hatāvaśeṣān utsṛjya tvadīyān kati cid rathān javenābhyadravad rājan dhanaṃjayarathaṃ prati
english: leaving behind the few chariots of your side that survived the slaughter, charged with speed, O king, toward Dhanaṃjaya's chariot.

sanskrit: tatas tat prādravat sainyaṃ hatabhūyiṣṭham āturam dṛṣṭvā yad arjunaṃ bhīmo jagāma bhrātaraṃ prati
english: Then that army, the greater part of it slain and stricken, took to flight, when it saw Bhīma go toward his brother Arjuna.

sanskrit: hatāvaśiṣṭāṃs turagān arjunena mahājavān bhīmo vyadhamad abhrānto gadāpāṇir mahāhave
english: The swift horses that had survived Arjuna's killing, Bhīma, mace in hand and unwavering, scattered in that great battle.

sanskrit: kālarātrim ivātyugrāṃ naranāgāśvabhojanām prākārāṭṭapuradvāradāraṇīm atidāruṇām
english: He wielded a mace fierce as the Night of Doom, a devourer of men and elephants and horses, a shatterer of ramparts and watchtowers and city gates, exceedingly dreadful.

sanskrit: tato gadāṃ nṛnāgāśveṣv āśu bhīmo vyavāsṛjat sā jaghāna bahūn aśvān aśvārohāṃś ca māriṣa
english: Then Bhīma swiftly hurled the mace among men and elephants and horses, and it slew many steeds and their riders, O honored one.

sanskrit: kāṃsyāyasatanutrāṃs tān narān aśvāṃś ca pāṇḍavaḥ pothayām āsa gadayā saśabdaṃ te 'patan hatāḥ
english: Those men and horses clad in armor of bronze and iron the Pāṇḍava crushed with his mace, and with a great noise they fell down slain.

sanskrit: hatvā tu tad gajānīkaṃ bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ punaḥ svaratham āsthāya pṛṣṭhato 'rjunam anvagāt
english: Having destroyed that elephant division, mighty Bhīmasena remounted his own chariot and followed in Arjuna's rear.

sanskrit: hataṃ parāṅmukhaprāyaṃ nirutsāhaṃ paraṃ balam vyālambata mahārāja prāyaśaḥ śastraveṣṭitam
english: The enemy's host, slain, all but turned in flight, drained of spirit, lingered there, O great king, for the most part encircled by weapons.

sanskrit: vilambamānaṃ tat sainyam apragalbham avasthitam dṛṣṭvā prācchādayad bāṇair arjunaḥ prāṇatāpanaiḥ
english: Seeing that army faltering, dispirited, and standing irresolute, Arjuna overwhelmed it with arrows that tormented the life-breath.

sanskrit: tataḥ kurūṇām abhavad ārtanādo mahāmṛdhe rathāśvanāgāsuharair vadhyatām arjuneṣubhiḥ
english: Then there arose among the Kurus a wail of anguish in that great battle, as they were slaughtered by Arjuna's shafts that stole the lives of chariot-warriors, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtaṃ bhṛśaṃ tasthau līyamānaṃ parasparam alātacakravat sainyaṃ tadābhramata tāvakam
english: Crying out in dismay, clinging close one to another, your army then whirled about like a circle traced by a firebrand.

sanskrit: ādīptaṃ tava tat sainyaṃ śaraiś chinnatanucchadam āsīt svaśoṇitaklinnaṃ phullāśokavanaṃ yathā
english: That army of yours, set ablaze and stripped of its armor by the arrows, was drenched in its own blood, like a grove of aśoka trees in full crimson bloom.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā kuravas tatra vikrāntaṃ savyasācinaḥ nirāśāḥ samapadyanta sarve karṇasya jīvite
english: Seeing there the prowess of Savyasācin, the Kurus all grew hopeless of Karṇa's life.

sanskrit: aviṣahyaṃ tu pārthasya śarasaṃpātam āhave matvā nyavartan kuravo jitā gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: Deeming Pārtha's torrent of arrows unbearable in the fray, the Kurus turned back, vanquished by the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: te hitvā samare pārthaṃ vadhyamānāś ca sāyakaiḥ pradudruvur diśo bhītāś cukruśuś cāpi sūtajam
english: Abandoning Pārtha in the battle and mown down by his shafts, they fled in terror in all directions and cried out to the Sūta's son.

sanskrit: abhyadravata tān pārthaḥ kirañ śaraśatān bahūn harṣayan pāṇḍavān yodhān bhīmasenapurogamān
english: Pārtha pursued them, scattering many hundreds of arrows, gladdening the Pāṇḍava warriors led by Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: putrās tu te mahārāja jagmuḥ karṇarathaṃ prati agādhe majjatāṃ teṣāṃ dvīpaḥ karṇo 'bhavat tadā
english: But your sons, O great king, made for Karṇa's chariot; as they sank in fathomless waters, Karṇa then became their island.

sanskrit: kuravo hi mahārāja nirviṣāḥ pannagā iva karṇam evopalīyanta bhayād gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ
english: For the Kurus, O great king, like serpents drained of their venom, clung close to Karṇa alone, out of dread of the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: yathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni mṛtyor bhītāni bhārata dharmam evopalīyante karmavanti hi yāni ca
english: As all creatures that are bound to action, in their fear of death, O Bhārata, take refuge in dharma alone,—

sanskrit: tathā karṇaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ putrās tava narādhipa upālīyanta saṃtrāsāt pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: so did your sons, O ruler of men, in their terror of the great-souled Pāṇḍava, cling to Karṇa, that mighty archer.

sanskrit: tāñ śoṇitapariklinnān viṣamasthāñ śarāturān mā bhaiṣṭety abravīt karṇo hy abhito mām iteti ca
english: To them, drenched in blood, set in dire straits, tormented by arrows, Karṇa said: "Do not fear—come hither, to me, on every side."

sanskrit: saṃbhagnaṃ hi balaṃ dṛṣṭvā balāt pārthena tāvakam dhanur visphārayan karṇas tasthau śatrujighāṃsayā pāñcālān punar ādhāvat paśyataḥ savyasācinaḥ
english: Seeing your host broken by force at Pārtha's hands, Karṇa, twanging his bow, stood firm with intent to slay the foe, and charged once more upon the Pāñcālas before the very eyes of Savyasācin.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣaṇena kṣitipāḥ kṣatajapratimekṣaṇāḥ karṇaṃ vavarṣur bāṇaughair yathā meghā mahīdharam
english: Then in an instant the lords of earth, their eyes blood-red like wounds, rained floods of arrows upon Karṇa, as the clouds upon a mountain.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi karṇamuktāni māriṣa vyayojayanta pāñcālān prāṇaiḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ vara
english: Then thousands of arrows loosed by Karṇa, O honored one, parted the Pāñcālas from their lives, O best of living beings.

sanskrit: tato raṇo mahān āsīt pāñcālānāṃ viśāṃ pate vadhyatāṃ sūtaputreṇa mitrārthe 'mitraghātinām
english: Then there was a great battle, O lord of peoples, as the Pāñcālas, slayers of foes, were cut down by the Sūta's son for the sake of his friend.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ karṇaḥ kuruṣu pradruteṣu; varūthinā śvetahayena rājan pāñcālaputrān vyadhamat sūtaputro; maheṣubhir vāta ivābhrasaṃghān
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, when the Kurus had fled, Karṇa, the Sūta's son, O king, with his white-horsed, armored car, scattered the sons of the Pāñcālas with his mighty shafts, as the wind scatters the masses of clouds.

sanskrit: sūtaṃ rathād añjalikena pātya; jaghāna cāśvāñ janamejayasya śatānīkaṃ sutasomaṃ ca bhallair; avākirad dhanuṣī cāpy akṛntat
english: Felling Janamejaya's charioteer from the car with an añjalika shaft, he slew his horses; and with broad-headed arrows he overwhelmed Śatānīka and Sutasoma, and cut their bows asunder.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ nirbibhedātha ṣaḍbhir; jaghāna cāśvaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ tasya saṃkhye hatvā cāśvān sātyakeḥ sūtaputraḥ; kaikeyaputraṃ nyavadhīd viśokam
english: Then he pierced Dhṛṣṭadyumna with six arrows and slew his right-hand horse in the fight; and having killed the steeds of Sātyaki, the Sūta's son slew Viśoka, the son of the Kaikeya king.

sanskrit: tam abhyadhāvan nihate kumāre; kaikeyasenāpatir ugradhanvā śarair vibhinnaṃ bhṛśam ugravegaiḥ; karṇātmajaṃ so 'bhyahanat suṣeṇam
english: When the prince was slain, the Kaikeya commander, fierce of bow, charged upon him; pierced sorely by his swift and violent shafts, he in turn struck Suṣeṇa, Karṇa's own son.

sanskrit: tasyārdhacandrais tribhir uccakarta; prasahya bāhū ca śiraś ca karṇaḥ sa syandanād gām apatad gatāsuḥ; paraśvadhaiḥ śāla ivāvarugṇaḥ
english: With three crescent-headed arrows Karṇa forcibly severed both his arms and his head; and lifeless he fell from his chariot to the earth, like a śāla tree hewn down by axes.

sanskrit: hatāśvam añjogatibhiḥ suṣeṇaḥ; śinipravīraṃ niśitaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ pracchādya nṛtyann iva sautiputraḥ; śaineyabāṇābhihataḥ papāta
english: Suṣeṇa, the charioteer's grandson, his own horses slain, covered the hero of Śini's line with swift, keen shafts and seemed almost to dance; yet, struck by an arrow of the Śaineya, he fell.

sanskrit: putre hate krodhaparītacetāḥ; karṇaḥ śinīnām ṛṣabhaṃ jighāṃsuḥ hato 'si śaineya iti bruvan sa; vyavāsṛjad bāṇam amitrasāham
english: His son slain, his mind seized by wrath, Karṇa, eager to kill the bull of Śini's line, crying "You are slain, O Śaineya!" loosed an arrow that overcomes all foes.

sanskrit: sa tasya ciccheda śaraṃ śikhaṇḍī; tribhis tribhiś ca pratutoda karṇam śikhaṇḍinaḥ kārmukaṃ sa dhvajaṃ ca; cchittvā śarābhyām ahanat sujātam
english: But Śikhaṇḍin cut that arrow apart and struck back at Karṇa with three shafts after three; and Karṇa, cutting through Śikhaṇḍin's bow and banner, slew with two arrows the warrior Sujāta.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ ṣaḍbhir avidhyad ugro; dānto dhārṣṭadyumnaśiraś cakarta athābhinat sutasomaṃ śareṇa; sa saṃśitenādhirathir mahātmā
english: The fierce and self-controlled one pierced Śikhaṇḍin with six arrows and struck off the head of Dhṛṣṭadyumna's son; then the great-souled son of Adhiratha pierced Sutasoma with a whetted shaft.

sanskrit: athākrande tumule vartamāne; dhārṣṭadyumne nihate tatra kṛṣṇaḥ apāñcālyaṃ kriyate yāhi pārtha; karṇaṃ jahīty abravīd rājasiṃha
english: Then, amid the tumultuous wailing, when the son of Dhṛṣṭadyumna had been slain there, Kṛṣṇa said, O lion among kings: "The Pāñcālas are being unmade—go, O Pārtha, and slay Karṇa."

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasyāśu narapravīro; rathaṃ rathenādhirather jagāma bhaye teṣāṃ trāṇam icchan subāhur; abhyāhatānāṃ rathayūthapena
english: Then, laughing, the foremost of men swiftly drove his chariot against the chariot of Adhiratha's son, the strong-armed one desiring to shield those who were being struck down by that leader of chariot-hosts.

sanskrit: visphārya gāṇḍīvam athograghoṣaṃ; jyayā samāhatya tale bhṛśaṃ ca bāṇāndhakāraṃ sahasaiva kṛtvā; jaghāna nāgāśvarathān narāṃś ca
english: Twanging the dread-sounding Gāṇḍīva and striking the bowstring hard against the leather guard, making at once a darkness of arrows, he slew elephants and horses and chariots and men.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmaseno 'nu yayau rathena; pṛṣṭhe rakṣan pāṇḍavam ekavīram tau rājaputrau tvaritau rathābhyāṃ; karṇāya yātāv aribhir vimuktau
english: Bhīmasena followed him with his chariot, guarding from behind that lone hero among the Pāṇḍavas; and the two princes, hastening on their two cars, set forth against Karṇa, breaking free of the foe.

sanskrit: atrāntare sumahat sūtaputraś; cakre yuddhaṃ somakān saṃpramṛdnan rathāśvamātaṅgagaṇāñ jaghāna; pracchādayām āsa diśaḥ śaraiś ca
english: Meanwhile the Sūta's son waged a mighty battle, crushing the Somakas; he slew their hosts of chariots, horses, and elephants, and shrouded all the directions with arrows.

sanskrit: tam uttamaujā janamejayaś ca; kruddhau yudhāmanyuśikhaṇḍinau ca karṇaṃ vineduḥ sahitāḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ; saṃmardamānāḥ saha pārṣatena
english: Uttamaujas and Janamejaya, enraged, and Yudhāmanyu and Śikhaṇḍin, together with the son of Pṛṣata, assailed Karṇa with their shafts, crushing him in the press.

sanskrit: te pañca pāñcālarathāḥ surūpair; vaikartanaṃ karṇam abhidravantaḥ tasmād rathāc cyāvayituṃ na śekur; dhairyāt kṛtātmānam ivendriyāṇi
english: Those five Pāñcāla chariot-warriors, rushing upon Vaikartana Karṇa with their fair arrows, could not dislodge him from his chariot—no more than the senses can move a self-mastered man from his steadfastness.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dhanūṃṣi dhvajavājisūtāṃs; tūṇaṃ patākāś ca nikṛtya bāṇaiḥ tān pañcabhiḥ sa tv ahanat pṛṣatkaiḥ; karṇas tataḥ siṃha ivonnanāda
english: Cutting away their bows, their banners, horses, charioteers, quivers, and pennons with his arrows, Karṇa struck those five with five shafts and then roared like a lion.

sanskrit: tasyāsyatas tān abhinighnataś ca; jyābāṇahastasya dhanuḥsvanena sādridrumā syāt pṛthivī viśīrṇā; ity eva matvā janatā vyaṣīdat
english: As he shot at and smote them down, bowstring and arrow in hand, at the twang of his bow the people sank in dread, thinking, "Surely the earth, with its mountains and trees, is being shattered."

sanskrit: sa śakracāpapratimena dhanvanā; bhṛśātatenādhirathiḥ śarān sṛjan babhau raṇe dīptamarīcimaṇḍalo; yathāṃśumālī pariveṣavāṃs tathā
english: With his bow, drawn taut and likened to Indra's rainbow, the son of Adhiratha, loosing arrows, shone in battle with a halo of blazing rays, like the sun garlanded in light.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ parābhinac; chitaiḥ śaraiḥ ṣaḍbhir athottamaujasam tribhir yudhāmanyum avidhyad āśugais; tribhis tribhiḥ somakapārṣatātmajau
english: He pierced Śikhaṇḍin with twelve whetted arrows, and Uttamaujas with six; with three swift shafts he struck Yudhāmanyu, and with three each the sons of Somaka and of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: parājitāḥ pañca mahārathās tu te; mahāhave sūtasutena māriṣa nirudyamās tasthur amitramardanā; yathendriyārthātmavatā parājitāḥ
english: Those five great chariot-warriors, crushers of foes, vanquished by the Sūta's son in that great battle, O honored one, stood there bereft of effort, like the objects of sense overcome by a self-disciplined man.

sanskrit: nimajjatas tān atha karṇasāgare; vipannanāvo vaṇijo yathārṇave uddadhrire naubhir ivārṇavād rathaiḥ; sukalpitair draupadijāḥ svamātulān
english: As they were sinking in the sea that was Karṇa, like merchants with foundered ships upon the deep, the sons of Draupadī drew up their maternal uncles from the flood with their well-furnished chariots, as with boats from the ocean.

sanskrit: tataḥ śinīnām ṛṣabhaḥ śitaiḥ śarair; nikṛtya karṇaprahitān iṣūn bahūn vidārya karṇaṃ niśitair ayasmayais; tavātmajaṃ jyeṣṭham avidhyad aṣṭabhiḥ
english: Then the bull of Śini's line, cutting apart with keen shafts the many arrows sped by Karṇa, and rending Karṇa with whetted iron-tipped darts, struck your eldest son with eight.

sanskrit: kṛpo 'tha bhojaś ca tavātmajas tathā; svayaṃ ca karṇo niśitair atāḍayat sa taiś caturbhir yuyudhe yadūttamo; digīśvarair daityapatir yathā tathā
english: Then Kṛpa and the Bhoja and your son, and Karṇa himself, smote him with sharp arrows; and that best of the Yādavas fought against those four, as the lord of the Daityas against the guardians of the quarters.

sanskrit: samānateneṣvasanena kūjatā; bhṛśātatenāmitabāṇavarṣiṇā babhūva durdharṣataraḥ sa sātyakiḥ; śaran nabhomadhyagato yathā raviḥ
english: With his bow evenly drawn, humming, bent to its full and raining countless arrows, that Sātyaki grew ever harder to assail, like the sun risen to mid-heaven in autumn.

sanskrit: punaḥ samāsādya rathān sudaṃśitāḥ; śinipravīraṃ jugupuḥ paraṃtapāḥ sametya pāñcālarathā mahāraṇe; marudgaṇāḥ śakram ivārinigrahe
english: Regaining their chariots, the Pāñcāla warriors, well-armored scorchers of foes, rallying in that great battle, guarded the hero of Śini's line, as the host of Maruts guards Indra in the crushing of his enemies.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavad yuddham atīva dāruṇaṃ; tavāhitānāṃ tava sainikaiḥ saha rathāśvamātaṅgavināśanaṃ tathā; yathā surāṇām asuraiḥ purābhavat
english: Then there arose an exceedingly dreadful battle between your foes and your soldiers, destructive of chariots and horses and elephants, even as of old there was between the gods and the asuras.

sanskrit: rathadvipā vājipadātayo 'pi vā; bhramanti nānāvidhaśastraveṣṭitāḥ paraspareṇābhihatāś ca caskhalur; vinedur ārtā vyasavo 'patanta ca
english: Chariots and elephants, horsemen and footmen alike, wrapped about with weapons of every kind, wheeled to and fro; struck by one another they stumbled, cried out in anguish, and fell down lifeless.

sanskrit: tathā gate bhīmam abhīs tavātmajaḥ; sasāra rājāvarajaḥ kirañ śaraiḥ tam abhyadhāvat tvarito vṛkodaro; mahāruruṃ siṃha ivābhipetivān
english: In such a pass, your fearless son, the king's younger brother, advanced against Bhīma, scattering arrows; and Vṛkodara rushed swiftly upon him, as a lion springs upon a great ruru deer.

sanskrit: tatas tayor yuddham atītamānuṣaṃ; pradīvyatoḥ prāṇadurodare 'bhavat paraspareṇābhiniviṣṭaroṣayor; udagrayoḥ śambaraśakrayor yathā
english: Then between those two, gambling with life as their stake, there was a battle beyond the human, each fixed in fury upon the other, those two exalted ones, like Śambara and Indra of old.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ śarīrāntakaraiḥ sutejanair; nijaghnatus tāv itaretaraṃ bhṛśam sakṛtprabhinnāv iva vāśitāntare; mahāgajau manmathasaktacetasau
english: With body-ending, keenly sharpened arrows the two struck each other hard, like two great elephants in rut, their minds set on a single she-elephant between them, smiting again and again.

sanskrit: tavātmajasyātha vṛkodaras tvaran; dhanuḥ kṣurābhyāṃ dhvajam eva cācchinat lalāṭam apy asya bibheda patriṇā; śiraś ca kāyāt prajahāra sāratheḥ
english: Then Vṛkodara, hastening, cut your son's bow and his banner with two razor-edged arrows, pierced his brow as well with a feathered shaft, and struck the head of his charioteer from the body.

sanskrit: sa rājaputro 'nyad avāpya kārmukaṃ; vṛkodaraṃ dvādaśabhiḥ parābhinat svayaṃ niyacchaṃs turagān ajihmagaiḥ; śaraiś ca bhīmaṃ punar abhyavīvṛṣat
english: That prince, taking up another bow, pierced Vṛkodara with twelve arrows; and himself reining in his steeds, he once more rained straight-flying shafts upon Bhīma.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatrākarod duṣkaraṃ rājaputro; duḥśāsanas tumule yudhyamānaḥ ciccheda bhīmasya dhanuḥ kṣureṇa; ṣaḍbhiḥ śaraiḥ sārathim apy avidhyat
english: Saṃjaya said: There the prince Duḥśāsana, fighting in the tumult, performed a hard feat: with a razor-edged arrow he cut Bhīma's bow, and pierced his charioteer with six shafts.

sanskrit: tato 'bhinad bahubhiḥ kṣipram eva; vareṣubhir bhīmasenaṃ mahātmā sa vikṣaran nāga iva prabhinno; gadām asmai tumule prāhiṇod vai
english: Then the great-souled one swiftly pierced Bhīmasena with many choice arrows; but he, pouring forth blood like an elephant in rut, hurled his mace at him in the tumult.

sanskrit: tayāharad daśa dhanvantarāṇi; duḥśāsanaṃ bhīmasenaḥ prasahya tayā hataḥ patito vepamāno; duḥśāsano gadayā vegavatyā
english: With it Bhīmasena, by main force, swept Duḥśāsana away the space of ten bow-lengths; struck by that swift mace, Duḥśāsana fell down trembling.

sanskrit: hayāḥ sasūtāś ca hatā narendra; cūrṇīkṛtaś cāsya rathaḥ patantyā vidhvastavarmābharaṇāmbarasrag; viceṣṭamāno bhṛśavedanārtaḥ
english: His horses with their charioteer were slain, O king, and his chariot ground to powder by the falling mace; his armor, ornaments, garments, and garlands shattered, he writhed, racked with grievous pain.

sanskrit: tataḥ smṛtvā bhīmasenas tarasvī; sāpatnakaṃ yat prayuktaṃ sutais te rathād avaplutya gataḥ sa bhūmau; yatnena tasmin praṇidhāya cakṣuḥ
english: Then mighty Bhīmasena, recalling all the enmity that your sons had wrought, leapt down from his chariot and came to the ground, fixing his gaze with care upon him.

sanskrit: asiṃ samuddhṛtya śitaṃ sudhāraṃ; kaṇṭhe samākramya ca vepamānam utkṛtya vakṣaḥ patitasya bhūmāv; athāpibac choṇitam asya koṣṇam āsvādya cāsvādya ca vīkṣamāṇaḥ; kruddho 'tivelaṃ prajagāda vākyam
english: Drawing his keen, well-honed sword and treading upon the throat of the trembling man, he tore open the breast of the fallen one upon the ground, and drank his warm blood; and tasting it again and again and gazing about, wrathful beyond measure, he spoke these words:

sanskrit: stanyasya mātur madhusarpiṣo vā; mādhvīkapānasya ca satkṛtasya divyasya vā toyarasasya pānāt; payodadhibhyāṃ mathitāc ca mukhyāt sarvebhya evābhyadhiko raso 'yaṃ; mato mamādyāhitalohitasya
english: "Than a mother's milk, than honey or clarified butter, than well-prepared mead, than the taste of celestial water, than the choicest draught churned from milk and curds—sweeter than all of these, I deem, is this taste of the lifeblood of my enemy that I drink today."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ punar ādravantam; āsvādya valgantam atiprahṛṣṭam ye bhīmasenaṃ dadṛśus tadānīṃ; bhayena te 'pi vyathitā nipetuḥ
english: As he spoke thus and again rushed forward, tasting the blood and leaping in fierce exultation, those who beheld Bhīmasena then, shaken with terror, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: ye cāpi tatrāpatitā manuṣyās; teṣāṃ karebhyaḥ patitaṃ ca śastram bhayāc ca saṃcukruśur uccakais te; nimīlitākṣā dadṛśuś ca tan na
english: And those men there who did not fall—their weapons dropped from their hands, and they cried aloud in fear, and with closed eyes they would not look upon it.

sanskrit: ye tatra bhīmaṃ dadṛśuḥ samantād; dauḥśāsanaṃ tadrudhiraṃ pibantam sarve palāyanta bhayābhipannā; nāyaṃ manuṣya iti bhāṣamāṇāḥ
english: All who there beheld Bhīma on every side drinking the blood of Duḥśāsana fled, overtaken by terror, crying out, "This is no man!"

sanskrit: śṛṇvatāṃ lokavīrāṇām idaṃ vacanam abravīt eṣa te rudhiraṃ kaṇṭhāt pibāmi puruṣādhama brūhīdānīṃ susaṃrabdhaḥ punar gaur iti gaur iti
english: In the hearing of the heroes of the world he spoke these words: "This blood of yours I drink from your very throat, O basest of men. Now, in your high fury, say once again, 'A cow! A cow!'"

sanskrit: pramāṇakoṭyāṃ śayanaṃ kālakūṭasya bhojanam daśanaṃ cāhibhiḥ kaṣṭaṃ dāhaṃ ca jatuveśmani
english: "The sleep that you contrived at Pramāṇakoṭi, the feeding of the kālakūṭa poison, the cruel biting by serpents, the burning in the house of lac;—"

sanskrit: dyūtena rājyaharaṇam araṇye vasatiś ca yā iṣvastrāṇi ca saṃgrāmeṣv asukhāni ca veśmani
english: "the seizing of our kingdom by the game of dice, and the dwelling in the forest that followed, the arrows and weapons in the battles, and the miseries in our own house;—"

sanskrit: duḥkhāny etāni jānīmo na sukhāni kadā cana dhṛtarāṣṭrasya daurātmyāt saputrasya sadā vayam
english: "these sorrows we know, and never once any joy—we, ever, through the wickedness of Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with his sons."

sanskrit: ity uktvā vacanaṃ rājañ jayaṃ prāpya vṛkodaraḥ punar āha mahārāja smayaṃs tau keśavārjunau
english: Having spoken these words, O king, and won his victory, Vṛkodara, O great king, smiling, spoke again to Keśava and Arjuna both:

sanskrit: duḥśāsane yad raṇe saṃśrutaṃ me; tad vai sarvaṃ kṛtam adyeha vīrau adyaiva dāsyāmy aparaṃ dvitīyaṃ; duryodhanaṃ yajñapaśuṃ viśasya śiro mṛditvā ca padā durātmanaḥ; śāntiṃ lapsye kauravāṇāṃ samakṣam
english: "What I vowed against Duḥśāsana in battle, O heroes, all of that I have this day accomplished here. This very day I shall offer up the second sacrifice as well: slaughtering Duryodhana like a sacrificial beast, and crushing the head of that vile one with my foot, I shall win peace before the very eyes of the Kauravas."
